sections.category: SpaceXAI ships Grok 4.5, a Cursor-trained frontier model that co-locates the model layer and the coding harness in one vertically integrated product priced to undercut incumbents

bullets.body: SpaceXAI shipped Grok 4.5 on July 8, 2026, a frontier model aimed squarely at coding and agentic work rather than consumer chat, and notable less for a new capability ceiling than for how it was built: the model was trained jointly by SpaceXAI and Cursor, with trillions of tokens of Cursor's own coding data folded into training, and it ships the same day as the default in Cursor across desktop, web, iOS, CLI, and SDK. On the xAI developer API it lists at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens for the base model, with a faster variant at $4/$18, a 500K-token context window (down from Grok 4.3's 1M), and configurable low/medium/high reasoning effort. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index it lands at 54, ranking fourth of 168 models behind Fable 5 (60), Opus 4.8 (56), and GPT-5.5 (55) while posting the strongest agentic tool-use result on the board, and on the Coding Agent Index it scores 76 in Grok Build, matching GPT-5.5 in Codex and trailing the top Claude-Code result by a single point at a per-task cost near $2.49 and roughly 60% fewer output tokens than Opus 4.8. The lab also flagged a candid caveat, that an earlier snapshot of the Cursor codebase was accidentally included in training and inflated one internal coding benchmark, so it excluded that result from its headline claims. The signal for anyone tracking the coding-agent stack is that a frontier vendor is now co-training its model on a top-tier IDE-agent's usage data and shipping it as that agent's default, collapsing the model layer and the harness layer into a single product at a price point that undercuts the standalone incumbents.

sections.category: SK Hynix and CXMT launch back-to-back multi-billion-dollar memory-chip IPOs in the same week, moving the AI-infrastructure capital story one layer beneath the accelerator into HBM and DRAM

bullets.body: The AI memory-chip boom is pulling two of the sector's biggest names to public markets in the same week. SK Hynix filed to sell nearly 17.8 million American depositary receipts in a US listing that, per an offering expected to price July 10 and begin trading July 11, could raise roughly $28 billion and rank among the largest technology IPOs on record; the South Korean memory maker is riding first-quarter revenue up nearly 200% year-over-year and a share price up about 260% year-to-date on high-bandwidth-memory demand, amid a supply crunch analysts have taken to calling "RAMageddon." Days behind it, China's largest DRAM maker CXMT is launching a roughly 29.5 billion yuan ($4.3 billion) Shanghai listing, with book-building from July 15, after reporting first-quarter revenue up 700% year-over-year, according to coverage of the back-to-back offerings that notes SK Hynix's book was more than seven times oversubscribed. Both companies say proceeds will fund fab-capacity expansion and equipment upgrades to meet AI demand. The throughline is that the capital chasing AI infrastructure is moving one layer beneath the accelerator, into the memory that feeds it: DRAM and HBM makers are now commanding IPO demand on the same AI-scarcity thesis that has driven GPU vendors, and two mega-listings in a single week is a marker of how tight the memory supply chain has become.

sections.category: Sysdig details JADEPUFFER, the first ransomware intrusion run end-to-end by an autonomous AI agent, after an LLM-driven agent chained a known Langflow RCE into full credential theft and data encryption

bullets.body: Sysdig's Threat Research Team detailed JADEPUFFER, which it characterizes as the first documented ransomware intrusion executed end-to-end by an autonomous AI agent rather than a human operator. The attackers exploited CVE-2025-3248, a missing-authentication remote-code-execution flaw in Langflow (a popular visual builder for LLM agents, patched in version 1.3.0 and on CISA's exploited-vulnerabilities list since May 2025), then handed control to an LLM-driven agent that ran the full chain itself: reconnaissance, harvesting API keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, and Gemini alongside cloud and crypto-wallet credentials, lateral movement to separate database servers, a secondary exploit of a 2021 Nacos authentication bypass, encryption and deletion of 1,342 Nacos configuration entries, and persistence via scheduled tasks. Sysdig's tell that a model, not a person, drove the operation was roughly 600 distinct, purpose-built payloads carrying explanatory code comments in the style of LLM output. Because the ransom note demanded Bitcoin with no recoverable decryption key, the intrusion was destructive regardless of payment. The reason this matters beyond one victim is that it collapses the cost and skill floor of a full ransomware campaign to whatever an agent can be steered to do against an exposed, long-known CVE, reframing agentic AI from a productivity story into an offensive-tooling one and putting unpatched agent-framework servers squarely in the blast radius.

citations.label: The Hacker News - AI agent exploits Langflow RCE to automate ransomware (JADEPUFFER, Sysdig)

sections.category: CISA orders a two-day federal patch sprint after adding four actively exploited flaws to its catalog, led by a maximum-severity Adobe ColdFusion RCE weaponized within hours of disclosure

bullets.body: CISA added four actively exploited flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on July 8, 2026, and gave federal civilian agencies until July 10 to patch, an unusually short window that tracks how fast these bugs are being weaponized. The standout is CVE-2026-48282, a maximum-severity CVSS 10.0 path-traversal flaw in Adobe ColdFusion that leads to arbitrary code execution; a researcher tracking exploitation told reporters an attempt was observed within hours of public disclosure, from an IP geolocated to India, a near-instant patch-to-exploit gap. The batch also includes two more 10.0-rated unauthenticated file-upload RCEs in Joomla page-builder extensions (CVE-2026-56290 in Joomlack and CVE-2026-48908 in JoomShaper SP Page Builder) and, relevant for anyone running AI tooling, a lower-scored authorization-bypass in Langflow (CVE-2026-55255) that lets an authenticated user execute another user's agent flow, per CISA's advisory. The practical read is that three separate maximum-severity code-execution bugs across widely deployed enterprise and web platforms are being exploited simultaneously, and the ColdFusion timeline in particular argues that defenders no longer have days to patch a critical flaw once it is public; the interval is now measured in hours.

citations.label: The Hacker News - CISA adds 4 actively exploited Adobe, Joomla, and Langflow flaws to KEV (July 8 2026)

sections.category: Zeroth raises $74M led by Ant Group as China's humanoid-robot market scales on home and education demand, a different use-case center than the West's factory-floor humanoid pitch

bullets.body: Chinese humanoid-robotics startup Zeroth raised about $74 million in pre-Series A funding to scale its home embodied-AI business, in a round led by Ant Group with Geely Capital, 37 Interactive Entertainment, Hua Capital, and existing backer Monolith participating. The company says it has surpassed 30,000 robot orders and grew revenue roughly 600% year-over-year in the first half of 2026, selling its M1 and W1 robots into early-childhood education, smart-home, and pet-companionship uses rather than the factory and warehouse deployments that dominate the Western humanoid pitch. The round lands amid a broader surge in robotics financing and a distinctly Chinese pattern of consumer- and education-oriented embodied AI shipping in volume: where US humanoid programs emphasize industrial pilots, Zeroth's order book and growth rate point to home and education as the demand centers where Chinese vendors are booking real units now. It is a concrete data point that the humanoid market is bifurcating by geography and use case, not just by hardware capability.

citations.label: The AI Insider - China's humanoid robot maker Zeroth raises $74M pre-Series A (July 8 2026)

sections.category: AI events to plan around now: ICML's Seoul workshops close out the weekend while the chip, security, and enterprise tracks stack up from August into the fall

bullets.body: Research first: ICML 2026 in Seoul has wrapped its main program at COEX but its workshops run July 10-11, so the technical sessions are still live for on-site and remote attendees this weekend; the next marquee research venue after it is NeurIPS in Sydney in December. For Bay Area locals, the next AI Tinkerers San Francisco meetup is set for August in the usual working-demo format, and The AI Conference returns to Pier 48 in San Francisco September 29 to October 1 with tracks spanning agents, infrastructure, and applied AI, while Anyscale's Ray Summit runs a late-August program for AI-infra builders. On the AI-chip and hardware track, the nearest gathering is Hot Chips 2026 at Stanford on August 23-25, whose early-registration rate closes July 31 per the Hot Chips registration page, followed by the AI Infra Summit in Santa Clara on September 15-17. The AI-security block clusters in August: SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit is August 11-12 at the Ritz-Carlton in Half Moon Bay, Black Hat USA and DEF CON 34's AI Village land in Las Vegas in early August, OWASP Global AppSec USA follows in San Francisco on November 5-6, and Zenity's AI Agent Security Summit series continues for teams focused on agent-hijack and MCP-layer defense. On the enterprise track, Ai4 2026 runs August 4-6 at The Venetian in Las Vegas, the ACM AI Leadership Summit is August 30 to September 2 in Atlanta, GitHub Universe is October 28-29, and AWS re:Invent runs November 30 to December 4 in Las Vegas. The near-term actions are catching the ICML workshops through July 11, locking the July 31 Hot Chips early-rate deadline, and booking the August AI Risk Summit and Black Hat/DEF CON dates, which remain the natural venues for confidential-inference and secure-accelerator announcements this cycle.
